question: Can a model predict 2027 FA signed AAV better than the prior-AAV anchors the optimizer prices on today — proven in backtest before any switch?

bar.rule: Model replaces anchors as the optimizer input only if held-out MAE on signed AAV (train classes 2022+2023, test class 2024) is at least 10% lower than the prior-AAV anchor baseline's MAE on the same test players.
bar.status: UNTESTED — no fit was run; anchors remain the optimizer input, unchanged.

incumbent.price_basis: prior-contract AAV (Spotrac) — a last-price anchor, NOT a predicted 2027 price (same basis and label as Cycle 26)

signing_census.source: MLB Stats API transactions via Cycle 54 (data/unc1_availability_backtest.json)

survivorship.source: data/salaries_cots_2027.json contract strings, parsed by this script
survivorship.bias: Terms are recoverable ONLY for contracts still touching a 2027 payroll: class 2022 keeps 24 of ~1,645 signings, all >= 3 years; class 2023 keeps 18, all >= 3 years; class 2024 keeps 35, none 1-year — against a census dominated by short deals. A backtest on survivors cannot certify predictions for the full 2027 class.

inventory.source: MLB Stats API transactions, as committed in data/unc1_availability_backtest.json (Cycle 54)
inventory.holds: Signing census: player + signing date for every 'Signed as Free Agent' transaction, classes 2022-2024 (n_signed 1645 / 1849 / 1659; 5,153 total screened)
inventory.reason: Identity and dates only — the transactions feed carries no contract terms (no years, no dollars). It defines the classes; it cannot price them.

inventory.holds: 153 parseable signed-contract strings ('6 y/$210M (25-30)') with cb_2027_aav, out of 237 player rows on 2027 payrolls
inventory.reason: Survivors only: a contract appears only if it still touches a 2027 payroll. Class 2022 keeps 24 deals, ALL >= 3 years — every 1-2 year deal signed for 2023-24 expired before this snapshot and is invisible. Class 2024 keeps 35, none of them 1-year. Spans also mix extensions with FA signings (no signing-type field). Training or testing on survivors validates the model on long deals only, then applies it to a 251-man class full of short-deal candidates — a known selection mechanism, not a sample.
Same snapshot shape as Cot's: active 2027 contracts, no signing dates, no expired deals. It is the incumbent anchor source, not a training set.

inventory.holds: 142 hitters: ACTIVE 2027 contract salaries vs 2027 projections
inventory.reason: Its own design limit, recorded at build: anchors are active contracts, 'not newly signed FA contracts — no signing-date field exists in the repo.' Cross-section, not signings.
This is the class TO BE priced. prev_aav is the incumbent anchor; spotrac_market_aav is Spotrac's own unbacktested estimate — another model's output is not training data.
No committed artifact records historical FA signing terms.

missing_source.what: A complete per-class record of FA signing terms — player (MLBAM id), signing date / class, years, total $, signed AAV — covering expired short deals as well as live long ones.
readiness_criteria: >= 90% of each class's StatsAPI signing census matched to terms, per class, 2022-2024
1- and 2-year deals present in proportion (the survivor test: class min_years == 1)
extensions separable from FA signings (signing-type field or transaction join)
AAV stated or computable as total $ / years from the same record

candidate_routes.status: NOT YET OPENED — when it lands, verify FIRST whether its contracts coverage includes expired historical deals or only current rosters; current-roster-only does not close this gap.
BLOCKED — 403 (standing probe result); never routed around.
UNPROBED — editorial tracker tables; scraping method is an owner call, not taken unilaterally.

features: pre-signing projected WAR (the projection the repo holds for that class year; if a class year's projections are not held, prior-season actual performance — and the artifact says which)
prior AAV (a feature, never the answer)
model_design_preregistered.form: Ridge regression on ln(AAV) first — simple, inspectable; gradient boosting runs only if it beats ridge clearly on the same backtest.
model_design_preregistered.validation: Train classes 2022 + 2023 -> test held-out class 2024, exact class split, no shuffling across classes.
baselines: prior-AAV anchor on the same test players
model_design_preregistered.metrics: Held-out MAE in $M and %, model vs each baseline, on identical players.
switch_mechanics_if_bar_met: Write data/price_model_2027.json (per-player predicted AAV for the 251, spec, backtest table)
Re-run the Cycle 49 MILP on predicted prices (same pools / quotas / constraints)
Re-run Cycle 50 +/-20% sensitivity on the predicted prices
UNC-2 intervals stay attached to the anchor-priced run until re-derived on predicted prices — no re-derivation shortcuts
Dashboard headlines switch with a visible 'prices: model-predicted' label; anchor-priced results preserved as a labeled sensitivity (Cycle 52 swap pattern)
Dashboard change ships with its own release cut (Cycle 60 lesson)
